Background (class-0) log-likelihood at a fraction of the assay limit

Source: R/likelihood.R
background_loglik.Rd

The absence of the modelled process is not itself a mechanistic trajectory. In the viral application, class 0 is specified rather than estimated: measurements are taken to fluctuate about a floor set by the assay, by default half the limit of detection.

Usage

background_loglik(obs, sigma, floor = 0.5)

Arguments

obs

As in trajectory_loglik(); needs lod for censored rows.

sigma

Residual standard deviation on the \(\log_{10}\) scale. Use the same value as the class-1 likelihood: the two classes share one scale, so sensitivity to it acts on both.

floor

Fraction of the limit of detection taken as the background level. 0.5 reproduces the analysis in the accompanying manuscript.

Value

A named numeric vector of log class-0 likelihoods.

Details

Because the floor is a fixed fraction of the limit, every censored measurement contributes the same constant \(\log \Phi(-\log_{10}(\mathrm{floor})/\sigma)\) whatever limit was in force. A record consisting only of censored measurements therefore has a class-0 likelihood that depends on how many visits there were and not on which visits they were, so its Bayes factor is driven entirely by the class-1 term.

Examples

obs <- data.frame(id = c(1, 1, 2, 2), time = c(1, 3, 1, 3),
                  value = c(NA, 500, NA, NA), lod = 100,
                  censored = c(TRUE, FALSE, TRUE, TRUE))
background_loglik(obs, sigma = 1.19)
#>         1         2 
#> -1.957045 -1.022142
